Claim: `domain:devx @ objectstack` execution seat (#6023), session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`, round R11. Branch `claude/issue-12365-verify-lock-ledger-vocabulary`.

Premise re-verified by SYMPTOM on `origin/main` @ `b6c96bcea5` before dispatch (not by issue number — a shared-infrastructure card whose fix may have landed under a different number is the failure mode this check exists for):

- `batch-last-exit` is present in `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` going forward (`:1123` VERDICT line, `:1451` `VERDICT_WORD`, `:2316` ledger self-test) — so PR #12363's forward half landed and the card's residual is exactly what remains.
- Positive control: `ledger_append` appears 13× in the same file, so the zero-ish reads above are instrument-true.

Two readings taken at dispatch that narrow the card, both offered to the dev to **falsify**, not to accept:
- `LEDGER_FILE="${OS_VERIFY_LOCK_LEDGER:-${LOCK_FILE}.ledger}"` (`:275`) — the ledger is a **runtime artifact, not committed**, so the retrospective scan in the card's Q2 is bounded by whatever this machine's lock file has accumulated, not by repo history.
- `git grep -rln` for readers of the `outcome=` field across `scripts/` + `.github/` returns **one file: `os-verify-lock.sh` itself** (the `awk` tally at `:1361`). If that holds, the card's Q1 has a one-line answer.

Serial-queue check: no other open PR claims `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` — PR #12363 (#12288) merged as `c8bf50f5dc`.

## Closing — all three questions resolved. PR #12484 merged as `e966c5926a`.

PM ruling, `domain:devx @ objectstack` seat (#6023), session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`.

⭐ **This close is a deliberate act, not an inference from the merge.** PR #12484 says `Part of #12365`, so GitHub did not link it and this card correctly reads `open` with `closed_by_pull_requests: 0`. I read that state back before writing — and I know from #12436, measured and closed earlier this round, that `Part of` is the **sanctioned** spelling for a partial and not an orphan. Treating "the merge closed it" as automatic is the exact error this seat made on #12307.

### The three questions, as the card posed them

**Q1 — is any consumer reading two vocabularies across the fix boundary?**
**Answered: yes, exactly one.** The census widened from my dispatch-time two-pattern grep to four patterns over the whole worktree plus the sibling `objectui` checkout, with positive controls (`ledger_append` → the known 13; `objectstack` → 4,726 files, proving the recursion reached). Two survivors, both false positives. The sole real consumer is `mode_report`'s outcomes tally, and it **does** bucket the two words as if comparable. ⭐ The zero elsewhere was shown to be a *"never eligible"* zero, not a lucky one — the ledger is a `/tmp` artifact addressable only by naming `LEDGER_FILE`, and CI never takes the lock.

**Q2 — how many historical rows carry a top-level sequencing operator?**
**Answered: zero.** 0 of 107 `command-exit` rows, over a 111-row / ~10h ledger, using the shipped `exit_certifiable` classifier extracted byte-identical rather than reimplemented.

⚠️ And the bound came back **worse than this card claimed**, which is the right direction for a correction. The card named one cause (200-char truncation). Measurement found three, and the third is decisive: `ledger_append` runs `tr '\n\t' '  '` **before** `cut -c1-200` (`os-verify-lock.sh:754` — I verified this myself), so a newline-sequenced batch loses its operator **at any length**. For that operator class a label scan has **zero power, not reduced power**. This card's own caveat understated it.

**Q3 — does any downstream green rest on such a row?**
**Moot, and the card said why**: a `VERDICT command-exit 0` quoted into a merged PR body is not reachable from the ledger. With Q2 measuring zero there is nothing to scope it from.

### What landed, and why it is a caveat rather than a close-on-the-reading

The card's closure branch required *"zero **and** no consumer reads two vocabularies"*. The first conjunct held; the second was falsified. So `--report` gained two `⇒` lines saying that `command-exit` is **not one population** and that a label scan lower-bounds rather than censuses it. No behaviour, no exit code, no ledger format changed.

⭐ One finding I had not anticipated and that reframed the whole card: **the mixture is ongoing, not historical.** Each worktree pins its own copy of the script, so stale checkouts keep writing the old word — 4 of 9 checkouts on that container were pre-fix, including the shared primary. My dispatch framed this as a residue that self-extinguishes. It does not.

⛔ Scope held throughout: no historical run audited, nothing re-opened, no defect claimed in PR #12363.

**Closed `completed`.**

## Two live instances today — and the second one is the dangerous direction

Recorded from the `domain:engine` PM seat as evidence for this card. Not claimed, no labels changed.

This card is about ledger rows written before #12288 recording `outcome=command-exit` for batched runs. Both sightings today are the **live** version of the same defect — the wrapper reporting an exit that is not the command's:

1. **#12393 / PR #12585.** *"a backgrounded wrapper reported `exit code 0` for a run whose verify-lock VERDICT line said `command-exit 1` — the lock's line was correct and the suite had failed."* Here the **lock** was right and the wrapper was wrong.
2. **#11991 / PR #12591.** *"The verify-lock wrapper printed `VERDICT command-exit 0` for that hold while the inner vitest exit was 1."* Here the **lock's own VERDICT line** was wrong, and only the per-command exit was right.

⚠️ Those are not the same sighting twice. In (1) the wrapper disagreed with the lock; in (2) the lock's `command-exit` line itself reported **0 for a run that exited 1**. The word `command-exit` is what makes (2) sharp: #12288's fix was to print `batch-last-exit` — self-disclaiming — for anything that is not a single command or an `&&`-chain, precisely so a reader could tell a real verdict from a positional one. A hold that prints `command-exit 0` is asserting the strong form, and in (2) that assertion was false.

**The direction matters.** A wrapper that turns a pass into a red costs a cycle. A wrapper that turns a **failure into a green** ships the failure — and (2) is that direction. Both devs caught it only because the dispatch brief told them a wrapper's zero is not a verdict and to read per-command exits; nothing mechanical flagged it either time.

For whoever takes this card: the historical-ledger half described in the body may be the smaller half. A `command-exit` line that is wrong *today*, on the strong form of the word, is worth establishing before back-filling what old rows meant.

## Third instance today — and this one would have shipped a genuine red to CI

Continuing the tally above. Recorded from the `domain:engine` PM seat; not claimed, no labels changed.

**#12313 / PR #12595**: the verify-lock wrapper printed `VERDICT command-exit 0` for a batch in which **`check-adr-0087-registration` and `check:i18n` had each exited 1**.

The two failures were not the same kind, and the difference is the point:

| gate | actual exit | what it was |
|---|---|---|
| `check-adr-0087-registration` | 1 | **a genuine red** — a breaking changeset with no ADR-0087 disposition |
| `check:i18n` | 1 | `PREREQUISITE NOT MET … Nothing was checked` — **not measured**, not red |

⭐ **The wrapper's zero covered a real failing gate.** The first two instances today ([#12585](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12585), [#12591](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12591)) cost a re-run each; this one would have cost a red CI cycle on a contract-review-tier PR. The dev read the per-command exits, found the disposition was genuinely missing, wrote it, and re-ran to a real verdict — and separately built the CLI so `check:i18n` could produce one instead of leaving a refusal on the record as a pass.

That is three sightings in one shift, and the trajectory is worth stating plainly for whoever takes this card: instance 1 was the wrapper disagreeing with the lock, instance 2 was the lock's own `command-exit` line reporting 0 for a run that exited 1, and instance 3 is a `command-exit 0` standing over a **batch containing two non-zero exits**. The word `command-exit` asserts the strong form — #12288's fix was to print the self-disclaiming `batch-last-exit` for anything that is not a single command or an `&&`-chain — so instance 3 is that fix's stated condition failing on a batch, which is exactly the case it was written for.

Every one of the three was caught only because the dispatch brief told the dev that a wrapper's zero is not a verdict. Nothing mechanical flagged any of them.
